jbtxHHpX_u0.title: 20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying
jbtxHHpX_u0.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
jbtxHHpX_u0.summary: In '20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying' (published 27 Sep 2026), Joseph Hogue, CFA argues Meta's new Muse personal AI agent is the first real killer app for agentic AI — bringing agents to consumer spending — and maps the ~20 stocks it upends. He likes PayPal (bought back at ~$50 after the takeover-offer rejection cratered it; ~10x P/E vs 16x a year ago, stablecoin growth) and Shopify (Muse users find its merchants' products and check out via Shop Pay; the rails underneath if Muse becomes shopping's front door) as the 'winners to buy'. Expedia is a conditional rebound play: its Muse partnership could redirect bookings through Expedia at Booking's expense, and the stock trades at 16x earnings vs a 25x average — though he stays cautious on the whole travel-middleman group (TripAdvisor, Airbnb, Booking, -15% to -24% in a month). On the AI-build side he ranks four neo-clouds — Oracle, Nebius, CoreWeave, IREN — and takes another look only at Nebius (his pick): ~500% revenue growth, best debt-to-free-cash-flow (-1.8x), 9.8x growth-adjusted P/S — while flagging Oracle's force majeure on a 2.5GW New Mexico data center as 'the first crack in the entire AI boom'. He avoids brokerages (Schwab, Raymond James, LPL, Ameriprise), banks (BofA, JPMorgan) and insurers (Progressive, Allstate) — AI agents could replace advice fees and erode sticky deposit-sweep profits — plus subscription names exposed to AI-driven cancellations (Adobe, SiriusXM, Match, Peloton, Planet Fitness, crushed 15%). Meta itself he holds: great story but ~30% above its 5-year average valuation after the 30% three-week run. Other tickers discussed with no call: Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, Salesforce, ServiceNow, AppLovin, Amazon. Caption note: auto-captions garble 'CoreWeave' as 'Corvus', 'IREN' as 'Iron', and 'Marvell' as 'Marvel'; tickers here are corrected.

7Lm8O0CuvLs.title: AMD Just Spent $8.2 Billion on Its Next AI Bet!!
7Lm8O0CuvLs.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
7Lm8O0CuvLs.summary: In 'AMD Just Spent $8.2 Billion on Its Next AI Bet!!' (published 29 Sep 2026), Jose Najarro covers two big semiconductor headlines. First, Nvidia increased its share-repurchase authorization by $150 billion, bringing the remaining buyback program to $235 billion to be executed through fiscal 2028 — against barely $100 billion of buybacks over the past decade. He reads it as a major confidence signal: management believes the money will be worth much more in the future, and the stock trades at roughly 19x forward earnings (likely 16-17x, he argues, since analysts keep underestimating Nvidia's growth). He also covers Nvidia's open agent safety platform — an open-source OpenShell runtime plus a Sentry watchdog running on Bluefield 4 DPUs — and notes partners include Anthropic, SpaceX and Perplexity, with OpenAI conspicuously absent. He reports Anthropic has contracted 2.6 gigawatts of Nvidia AI infrastructure to date, with partner contracted value exceeding $180 billion, dismissing fears Anthropic is moving away from Nvidia. Second, AMD's $8.2 billion all-stock acquisition of World Labs, the AI model and research lab founded by AI pioneer Dr. Fei-Fei Li (auto-captions garble her name as 'FFly'/'Dr. Lee'), expected to close by end of 2026. He frames it as a talent acquisition that gives AMD a front-row view of how AI workloads are evolving, informing its hardware/software roadmap and potential moves into robotics and physical AI. He applauds the all-stock structure — less than 1% of the company — as smarter than spending cash, while flagging one worry: AMD is already juggling software-stack improvements (ROCm), the Helios ramp, and a full-stack build-out, so this is one more thing on the plate. He trusts Lisa Su's judgment and expects the deal to look obviously smart in a year or two. Calls: NVDA — BUY (excited as an investor; buyback confidence; cheap forward P/E; $5T market cap noted); AMD — BUY (smart talent grab, trusts management; ~$67 per garbled captions). Other tickers discussed without calls: INTC and ARM (as compute platforms for the agent safety runtime), META (as an AMD partner), plus non-tradeable OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX and Perplexity.

gkt3BnXJf9s: Joseph Hogue, CFA — 'My New Favorite Stocks for AI Growth AND Income' (published 29 Sep 2026). Pitch: income investors no longer have to choose between AI-driven growth and cash flow. Hogue argues new YieldMax option-income ETFs let holders capture semiconductor upside while converting industry volatility into distributions. He walks through four: (1) CHPY — YieldMax Semiconductor Portfolio Options Income ETF, holding 15-30 semiconductor names and using a call-spread strategy targeting ~40% annualized distribution with weekly payouts (range this year $0.38-$0.71/share). (2) SOXY — the YieldMax Target 12 semiconductor fund, a growth-leaning counterpart targeting 12% income so more upside stays in the portfolio (monthly payouts, $0.65 to over $1/share this year). (3) AMDY — a single-stock AMD options-income ETF for a tactical overweight on AMD, which he says he bought early last year and has since cashed. (4) NVDY — the single-stock Nvidia version targeting a 47% distribution rate. Suggested builds: max income = 70% CHPY / 15% NVDY / 15% AMDY; income-plus-growth = 50% SOXY / 25% AMDY / 25% NVDY. He flags the risks: distributions fluctuate with premiums and volatility, and income is never guaranteed. Calls made: CHPY BUY (~40% target), SOXY BUY (12% target), AMDY BUY, NVDY BUY (47% target). Other tickers discussed: MU (up ~1,200% over 5 years), MRVL (~+400%), NVDA (10x), ARM — all mentioned only as semiconductor theme leaders held inside the ETFs, not as direct calls. Note: captions rendered the second fund's ticker as 'SOX Y', with garbled repeats as 'SOXW' and 'SOXL' later in the video — the described product is consistently the Target 12 fund. The video is sponsored by YieldMax, disclosed in-video.
_X0c2A-Ln9c: Travis Hoeft (Asymmetric Investing) — 'Risk Warning: 5 Stocks to Sell Before It's Too Late' (published 29 Sep 2026). Core thesis: five of the market's most popular AI-related stocks are vastly overvalued, and their improved financials are a mirage because AI capex doesn't hit the income statement until assets are in use. The common thread is deteriorating credit: borrowing costs are rising both market-wide and company-specific, execution is stumbling, and debt markets could eventually close to these names. (1) ORCL SELL — Oracle is down 53% over the past year; trailing-12-month free cash flow is -$28B against nearly $120B of debt, the 10-year borrowing rate has risen from 5.7% in February to ~7.3%, and the Project Jupiter data center invoking force majeure is 'not normal' — a sign of real execution problems behind $664B of remaining performance obligations. (2) CRWV SELL — CoreWeave carries a $47B market cap on just $7.6B of trailing revenue, $35B of debt, and burned -$5.7B of free cash flow in Q2 2026 alone; its June 2026 8.5% notes now yield over 12%, ROIC is negative. (3) MU SELL — take profits on Micron ($1.2T market cap): the ~7x forward P/E looks cheap only if 83-86% gross margins hold, but memory is a commodity — capacity lands in 2028-29, chip designs are shifting away from expensive HBM, and margin reversion to 40% would wipe out ~90% of profits. (4) AMZN SELL — retail growth has slowed (~13% TTM) and its $39B of retail operating profit is essentially the advertising business, which is threatened by agentic AI shopping (Muse/ChatGPT buy without viewing ads); estimated -$34B free cash flow in 2026, 26x forward P/E. (5) TSLA SELL — revenue flat for three years, operating margins down to 2-4.2% (a regular automaker), trading at 13x sales / 192x forward earnings, with ~$26B of capex expected to exceed operating cash flow, while Musk's attention shifts to SpaceX. Notable: two days after Joseph Hogue rated ORCL and CRWV AVOID on this same watch, Hoeft escalates both to outright SELL. Captions render CoreWeave as 'Cororeweave' throughout — ticker CRWV confirmed against the company discussed.

sY9DIuxZzmc.title: Why I Plan To Continue Buying Meta Stock
sY9DIuxZzmc.creator: Daniel Pronk
sY9DIuxZzmc.summary: In 'Why I Plan To Continue Buying Meta Stock' (published 30 Sep 2026), Daniel Pronk returns from two weeks in Italy to reassure viewers asking whether Meta's ~30% rally from the lows has made it expensive. His answer: no — his DCF still shows a $827 fair value on conservative inputs (15% annual operating-cash-flow growth, 14x price/OCF) and ~$1,000 on realistic ones (20% growth, 15x OCF, still below the 16x historical median), implying 15-22.6% annualized returns over three years. The video's first half is a long showcase of Meta's new Muse AI agent: over 3 million US downloads in 9 days, #1 on the App Store for two weeks, adopted faster than ChatGPT, and Pronk's own daily use cases — sponsorship email triage, media kits, and home-purchase paperwork, all via email access. He argues Muse rides Meta's free distribution across Instagram and WhatsApp, and its clearest monetization is harvesting user data to sharpen ad targeting. He is skeptical of Zuckerberg's 'savings-shared' monetization model (Muse touches no transaction) and unconvinced agentic AI will fully disrupt Amazon/Booking.com advertising — window-shopping behavior persists. On Meta Connect: Muse at the center, the teased 'watermelon' frontier model, impressive new VR glasses, and a questionable Meta Charm pocket device. Call: META — BUY (adding), still undervalued at ~23x next year's earnings; he will add when post-house-closing liquidity frees up. No other tickers called.

989CUhoOUg8.title: Buffett's "Going to Hell" Warning [5 Stocks to Buy Before It Gets Worse]
989CUhoOUg8.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
989CUhoOUg8.summary: In 'Buffett's "Going to Hell" Warning [5 Stocks to Buy Before It Gets Worse]' (published 30 Sep 2026), Joseph Hogue, CFA frames a Warren Buffett warning about part of the market 'going to hell' around the 10-year Treasury hitting a 24-year high. He attributes surging rates to four forces: persistent inflation (gas-driven CPI +3.4%), Uncle Sam's $2 trillion deficit, an AI-debt boom (Goldman sees hyperscaler debt issuance at a record $420B next year), and unexpectedly strong economic growth (flash PMI at a 5-year high) forcing the Fed toward more hikes. Five stocks to buy for this regime: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) — ~$360B in cash and T-bills collecting tens of billions at high rates, with financials/insurers in its portfolio earning more interest income; CME and CBOE — both down up to 17% last month on prediction-market competition fears, beneficiaries of rate-uncertainty hedging volume with a near-term bounce coming; the VanEck gold miners ETF (GDX) as a safety bet on inflation, deficits, and dollar weakness; and Vanguard's long-term bond ETF (BLV) — a conditional buy ("a little early"), attractive once rates level off, with a ~5% dividend and a possible bounce to $70 in the next recession. Six stocks to avoid: high-debt JBLU (debt/equity 591%, negative operating cash flow) and CCL (down 26% YTD, a falling knife), plus housing-chain DHI, PHM, BLDR, and Z as mortgage rates top 7%. Notable stance flip: Bank of America (BAC) moves from AVOID (Sep 28, long-term AI threat to financials) to BUY here — Hogue explicitly splits the time horizon: rate income now, AI disruption later. Sponsored Kalshi per-futures segment and a note that he is 'deeply invested in Ethereum' are mentions, not calls.

Ad2Pn32TWSs.title: Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!
Ad2Pn32TWSs.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
Ad2Pn32TWSs.summary: In 'Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!' (published 1 Oct 2026, covering Micron's Sep 30 post-close print), Jose Najarro — who does not own the stock — argues the triple beat (revenue, EPS, and next-quarter guidance all well above consensus) leaves Micron cheap, with the flat after-hours reaction reflecting already-high hopes. His bull case: pricing is doing the heavy lifting (DRAM revenue +27% YoY, NAND +42%, on only mid-single-digit bit growth), and Micron expects a tight market through 2027-28 even with mid-20s industry bit-shipment growth; 35% of revenue through 2030 is covered by multi-year take-or-pay contracts, with $150B of remaining performance obligations (at minimum contract prices, so the real figure could be much higher) and $32B in customer cash deposits. HBM repricing begins at the start of calendar 2027, Q1 is the gross-margin floor, and buybacks unlock after December 9 (the CHIPS Act incentive 2-year anniversary) — he would not be surprised by a $50B repurchase authorization. Watch items: DRAM sequential price growth is decelerating (from ~60% to the high teens), consumer PC/phone units face double-digit declines in 2026, and capex is stepping up past $50B in 2027 (funded by contracted demand, he stresses). Caveat: auto-captions heavily garble the reported figures (e.g. '$54.2 billion in revenue', '$33 in one quarter' EPS, '$60 to 63 billion' guide) — treat all numbers here as approximate. Call: MU — BUY ('still dirt cheap'), with a rerating as the prize and supply-tight AI demand as the engine. Also bullish on the wider semiconductor/neocloud space as a memory bottleneck 'extends the cycle'.

WHzxbGZoTPQ.title: Unloved Chinese Stocks - Value, Buy for 2X?
WHzxbGZoTPQ.creator: Sven Carlin
WHzxbGZoTPQ.summary: Sven Carlin works through the ~20 largest holdings of the China internet ETF - unloved after 13 years with no performance - screening for value: low P/Es, high cash flows, profitability and growth. Tencent (P/E ~15, dividends, buybacks, double-digit growth) is "interesting" on his buy-the-bad-mood/sell-the-exuberance framework; he owns Prosus as his Tencent proxy. JD.com he owns outright - the investment/profitability cycle swings 50-70%, with very high cash flow per share, dividend, 3.7% buyback yield and a logistics moat. Kuaishou is his standout free bet: core business at P/E ~7 with 68% ownership of Kling AI (raised ~$3B, growing 200%). Baidu trades near book value of its cash with AI/robotaxi optionality; Trip.com at P/E 10 with ~RMB 14B cash looks interesting; Tencent Music is cheap and profitable. Alibaba is "too high now" on declining legacy cash flows; NetEase and Lenovo are fairly priced holds. He avoids KE Holdings (P/E 26, frozen transaction market), Bilibili, GDS and Kingsoft Cloud. Overall: buy big-cap Chinese internet on weakness for ~50% minimum over three years, hold via ETF or directly, size ~10-15% of a global value portfolio - and only for European investors; he explicitly warns US investors off due to sanction/illiquidity risk (VIE structure, Taiwan). Note: auto-captions garble several names (Meituan as "Mu1", Kling AI as "Cling AI", renminbi as "raimi/remimi") - treat P/E and cash figures as approximate.

F6ds1vqtOTY.title: A Once in a Lifetime Financial Reset is Coming. (Why Stocks Are Next)
F6ds1vqtOTY.creator: Tom Nash
F6ds1vqtOTY.summary: Tom Nash reframes the "market crash is coming" narrative: a crash is certain, but the wrong question is 'will it crash?' - the right ones are whether your portfolio is protected and set up to profit from it. He walks through historical playbooks (1973 oil embargo, 1990 Iraq war, 2022 Ukraine) showing crashes followed by multi-year recoveries, and the volatility stats that make staying invested work (54% of days, 75% of years, 95% of decades, 100% of 20-year periods positive). His system: 12-month emergency fund, kill expensive debt, max tax-advantaged accounts, zero leverage, then a portfolio stress test using beta (a 50/50 S&P/Palantir portfolio falls ~60% in a 30% S&P drop). Stock selection: a big S&P 500 core as the "undefeated cheat code", elite businesses run through a 125-point scorecard, max 10 positions, dollar-cost average and double down on the way down (he bought Palantir at $6-9 in 2022). Emotions are the portfolio killer: 24-hour cooldown rule, don't check daily, write a personal "constitution". No explicit stock calls - Palantir, Tesla and Nvidia appear only as high-beta stress-test examples; the actionable recommendation is SPY as the core holding. Ends with a pitch for his free "panic-proof guide" and the academy (patreon.com/theMASH).
